title: Ectopic (focal) atrial tachycardia
summary: A focus in the atrium fires faster than the sinus node and takes over: abnormal automaticity.

events.label: Atrial focus
events.caption: An abnormal focus in the left atrium (tinted) fires on its own, faster than the sinus node, and the sinus node is overridden. This is abnormal automaticity.
events.ecg: A P wave of different shape from the sinus P wave, because the atria are activated from a different place.

events.label: Spread through the atria
events.caption: The impulse spreads from the focus across both atria.

events.label: Conducted to the ventricles
events.caption: Each impulse is conducted through the AV node, so the QRS is narrow.
events.ecg: A regular narrow-complex tachycardia with a P wave before each QRS.

events.label: Regular rate
events.caption: The focus fires regularly, here about 150 per minute.

teaching_points: Abnormal automaticity: pacemaker cells or other atrial cells generate impulses at a faster rate (slide 48).
Ectopic atrial tachycardia is regular, with a P wave of abnormal shape before each QRS (slides 58-59).
It differs from AV nodal reentry because the atrium is activated before the ventricle by a focus, not in a circuit.
